implementation_notes: Ruby 2.6 added functional composition to Proc and Method: `f >> g` returns a proc that calls f and then g, `f << g` calls g first, and anything responding to `call` can take part (ruby-doc.org; the feature is Feature #6284). The classic combinator therefore needs no code at all - the operators are the structure - and a composed proc is an ordinary value that can be stored in a constant, passed as `map(&chain)` or used in a block-based DSL. Hand-built composition remains only for older Rubies or for arity adaptation through curry, method objects or to_proc.
pitfalls: The operators chain only objects that respond to call: a Symbol must be written `:body.to_proc` first, while other objects with a call method chain directly.
Direction is easy to invert: `>>` applies left then right, `<<` right then left; treat one convention as house style and review chains against the docs.
Lambdas enforce arity, so a lambda step expecting one argument raises ArgumentError when a previous step yields several values (a proc would silently take the first).
